content:
jordan: FYI noticed a handful of orgs suddenly showing 'edit' permission in project list after the role-alias refactor deploy (role-refactor-2026-03-21). Small blast radius but likely by design mistake in alias expansion.

tess: can you share repro?

jordan: steps: switch to a user with role 'viewer-legacy', open /projects -> three-dot menu shows Rename/Delete. API permission endpoint returns {"can_view": true, "can_edit": true}. Expected can_edit false.

jordan: quick curl:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://console.internal/api/v1/projects/5678/permissions | jq .
# -> { "can_view": true, "can_edit": true, "derived_from": "role_alias:viewer-v2-expanded" }
```

liam: interesting, derived_from field shows alias expansion to viewer-v2-expanded which apparently includes editor in its set. That alias was created during the refactor to preserve legacy access.

kms-audit: NOTE: alias remap event kms:alias_update applied 2026-03-20T03:12:01Z for alias viewer->viewer-v2-expanded. No decrypt errors.

sec-bot: ALERT: unexpected_privilege_increase detected for 6 users across 2 orgs. Link: https://incident.internal/IR-2026-2997 severity LOW-MEDIUM.

tess: mitigation plan options: 1) quick alias rollback in KMS registry (atomic) 2) server-side policy filter to strip editor perms when role==viewer legacy 3) UI hide for risky affordances until policy reconciled

liam: we can rollback alias mapping in KMS but that requires key rotation window and will touch other services. Might be disruptive for customers using the new mapping.

jordan: I can push a server-side patch to the permissions service to treat role_alias=viewer-legacy as strict_viewer until we complete policy re-eval. That is low risk and hotfixable.

ops-bot: deploy request created: perms-hotfix-4765 -> pipeline #1204 triggered.

liam: also noticed audit logging didn't record the original bind mutation for a subset of users (some binds show role_delta but no actor). This makes customer-facing audit queries incomplete.

kms-audit: Confirmed: 4 alias_update events have incomplete metadata due to truncated payload in the remap job (remap-job-23). We're attaching raw logs.

jordan: we need two parallel tracks: 1) stopgap filter + deploy (hours) 2) full backfill to recompute derived permissions and emit complete audit entries (longer, maybe a day). Can we schedule backfill?

tess: schedule backfill: backfill-rbac-recompute-4765 queued, estimated runtime 6h for orgs impacted. Include audit write step to ensure customers see explicit audit entries.

sec-bot: RECOMMENDATION: revoke short-lived sessions for affected orgs OR force token refresh. TTL for session cache is 10m; some clients may keep edit affordances until expiry.

liam: running policy-sim locally against sample org Y now, will post diff.

jordan: UI patch merged to canary: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/pull/4540 includes `affordance_strict_mode` flag for legacy viewers.

ops-bot: perms-hotfix-4765 deployed to canary at 2026-03-21T06:12:00Z. Monitoring perf and perm-events.

tess: after hotfix, please verify audit entries generated by backfill and attach to incident IR-2026-2997. Also recommend a brief postmortem focusing on alias-life-cycle docs and KMS remap job validation.

liam: policy-sim result: 6 users had derived editor perms due to alias expansion rule `expand: include_editor=true`. Changing that flag to false removes editor from derived set.

jordan: agreed next steps (owners):
- hotfix server-side strict_viewer filter -> deployed to canary (jordan)
- schedule + run backfill for recompute & audit write -> queued (tess)
- KMS remap audit + patch remap job to include full metadata -> liam/kms-audit
- decide on alias rollback vs remap patch (ops owners) -> follow-up meeting
- revoke/force-refresh tokens for affected orgs -> security decision (sec team)

sec-bot: ACTIONS logged to IR-2026-2997. Please update incident with any customer contacts.

jordan: closing loop here for now. If anyone still sees edit affordances after cache TTL + hotfix, DM me user_id/org_id. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
